// Command escaper is a deliberately hostile wasm guest. It is compiled by
// rootfs's integration test and tries every way it can think of to read a file
// outside the directory forge mounted for it. Each attempt prints one line:
// "BLOCKED <path>" or "ESCAPED <path> <contents>".
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
)

func main() {}

//go:wasmexport attempt
func attempt() int32 {
	escapes := []string{
		"/work/../secret.txt",
		"/work/../../secret.txt",
		"/work/../../../etc/passwd",
		"/etc/passwd",
		"/work/sub/../../secret.txt",
		"/work/sub/./../../secret.txt",
		"/work/rel-escape",
		"/work/abs-escape",
		"/work/sub/up",
	}

	// Plant a fresh symlink at runtime and try to follow it, too.
	if err := os.Symlink("../secret.txt", "/work/planted"); err == nil {
		escapes = append(escapes, "/work/planted")
	}

	var escaped int32
	for _, p := range escapes {
		b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
		if err == nil {
			fmt.Printf("ESCAPED %s %q\n", p, string(b))
			escaped++
			continue
		}
		fmt.Printf("BLOCKED %s\n", p)
	}

	// A write outside the jail must fail too.
	if err := os.WriteFile("/work/../pwned.txt", []byte("x"), 0o644); err == nil {
		fmt.Println("ESCAPED write /work/../pwned.txt")
		escaped++
	} else {
		fmt.Println("BLOCKED write /work/../pwned.txt")
	}

	// Sanity: the legitimate file must be readable, or the test proves nothing.
	if b, err := os.ReadFile("/work/hello.txt"); err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("BROKEN legitimate read failed: %v\n", err)
		escaped++
	} else {
		fmt.Printf("OK legitimate read %q\n", string(b))
	}
	return escaped
}
